changes: Removed p1 'Manaharṣa': 'manaharṣana duntā juro' is best read as 'offered with joy of mind' (mana-harṣa-na), not a personal name; the donor is not named.

Beneficiary: 'muktā juna' is read as Newari 'mukta juna' ('when he died'), so the personal name of the śākyabhikṣu is probably not given. Name set to unnamed and confidence lowered to low; 'Mukta' as a name is kept only as an alternative in notes. The vihāra name is given as written because the reading is uncertain.
Scribe kept with a fragmentary name. Notes now say that '(++++)rayā na' may be a name ending in -ra followed by the ergative -na.
Place: notes say this is where the book was offered (the Lokeśvara/Ādinātha shrine on Kacchapagiri, Chobhar). It is not necessarily where the copy was made.
Purpose made more precise: offered for the welfare in the next world of a deceased śākyabhikṣu.

persons.name: [unnamed]
persons.evidence: śrōvacchavāhārayā śrīsākyābhikṣu muktā juna, paralokārthana duntā juro

purpose: offered (duntā) at the Lokeśvara shrine of Chobhar for the welfare in the next world (paralokārtha) of a deceased śākyabhikṣu
notes: The era is not stated. NS is taken from the catalogue and the Newari context: NS 788 ≈ 1668 CE. The second colophon repeats 'saṃvat 788'. The weekday was not checked. 'ānandā(vitā)keśvara' is probably Ānandādi-Lokeśvara, i.e. the Ādinātha Lokeśvara of Chobhar (Kacchapagiri, Covāhāra). This is the place of dedication and not necessarily the place of copying. 'manaharṣana' is taken as 'with a joyful mind'; reading it as the donor name Manaharṣa + ergative is less likely. 'mukta juna' = 'having died / when he died'. The alternative reading, a śākyabhikṣu named Muktā(-ju), cannot be ruled out. The vihāra 'śrōvacchavāhāra' is corrupt and cannot be identified. The scribe's name is lost in a lacuna ('(++++)rayā na'), probably a name ending in -ra followed by the ergative -na. Whether the scribe also made the offering is unclear.
